title: Definition
body_md:
A discrete channel is {\em symmetric} if the channel output alphabet can be partitioned into
subsets such that, within each subset, the matrix of transition probabilities satisfies the following: each row (resp.
column) is a permutation of each other row (resp. column).
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md: A symmetric channel $W \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{Y}\mid \mathcal{X})$ is  {\em singular} if $W (y\mid x) =W (y\mid z) = : w(y)$ for all $(x, y, z) \in \mathcal{X}\times \mathcal{Y}\times \mathcal{X} $ such that $W(y\mid x)W(y\mid z) >0$. Otherwise, it is {\em nonsingular}.

title: Remark
body_md:
For symmetric channels, both the minimum and maximum of $U(p,W)$ over $p\in\Pi$ are equal. In particular, $V_\epsilon(W)$ is independent of $\epsilon\in(0,1)$ --- see Lemma \ref{lemma:capacity_dispersion}. For simplicity, we denote this common value by $V(W)$.

    Moreover, for {\em nonsingular} channels, the dispersion $V(W)$ is strictly positive: $V(W)>0$.

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $\epsilon \in (0,1)$ and consider a random variable $X$ taking values in a finite input set, $\mathcal{X}$, with p.m.f. $p_X \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$. We refer to common randomness as a random variable $U \perp\!\!\!\!\!\!\perp X$ taking values in a set $\mathcal{U}$ with a probability distribution $p_U\in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{U})$.

An encoder, $f$, is a map $f: \mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{U} \mapsto [M],$
    where $M \in \mathbb{N}$ and $[M]$ representing a $M$-sized codebook. Similarly, a decoder, $g$, is a map $g:[M] \times \mathcal{U} \mapsto \mathcal{Y}.$

    We refer to a tuple $(f, g, U)$ as a size-$M$ $\epsilon$-simulation code for the ``target'' channel $W \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{Y}\mid \mathcal{X})$ if ${(X, Y) \sim p_X \tilde{W}_{Y\mid X}}$ where $Y  = g(f(X, U), U)$ and $\tilde{W} \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{Y}\mid \mathcal{X})$ such that $\Delta(\tilde{W}, W) \leq \epsilon$.

title: Definition
body_md:
The minimum channel simulation codebook size with fixed TV distance tolerance ${\epsilon \in (0,1)}$ is 

        $$M_\epsilon^*(W) := \min\{M\in \mathbb{N}: \exists \text{ a size-$M$ $\epsilon$-simulation code for } W \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{Y}\mid \mathcal{X})  \}.$$
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $I$ be a uniform random variable taking values in a $N$-sized message set $[N]$ with $N \in \mathbb{N}$. A ($N$) code for channel $W\in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{Y}\mid\mathcal{X})$, say $(f, \phi)$, consists of an encoder map $f:[N] \mapsto \mathcal{X}$ and a decoder map $\phi:\mathcal{Y} \to [N]$. 
    
    We let $\{\mathcal{A}_m\}_{m=1}^{[N]}$ denote the decoding regions and $\bar{P}_e(f, \phi, W)$ the average error probability of $(f, \phi)$ for channel $W$:

    $$\bar{P}_e(f, \phi):= \frac{1}{N}\sum_{m \in [N]}\sum_{y\in \mathcal{A}_m^c} W(y\mid f(m)).$$


The minimum average error probability
attainable by any $(N)$ code for $W$ is denoted by $\bar{P}_e(N, W)$. Then, for any $\epsilon \in (0,1)$, the largest number of distinct messages that can be transmitted through $W$ with tolerance $\epsilon$ is

$$N_\epsilon^*(W) := \max\{ N\in \mathbb{N}: \bar{P}_e(N, W) \leq \epsilon\}.$$

title: Proof
body_md:
The result will follow from matching upper and lower bounds for $\log M_\epsilon^*(W^{\otimes n})$. 
    
    We begin with the lower bound.
    Fix $\epsilon\in(0,1)$, and let
$$p=1-\epsilon,\qquad \delta_n=\frac1{\sqrt n},\qquad \alpha_n=p-\delta_n.$$
Choose
$$h=\frac{1}{2}\min\{\epsilon,1-\epsilon\}, \qquad E_\epsilon=[p-h,p+h]\subset(0,1),$$
and write
$$D_\epsilon=\sup_{v\in E_\epsilon}(\Phi^{-1})'(v)<\infty.$$
Then we clearly have $\alpha_n\in E_\epsilon$ eventually, and Lemma~\ref{lem:new} applies.
Define
$$G_\epsilon(n)=nC(W)+\sqrt{nV(W)}\,\Phi^{-1}(1-\epsilon).$$
The mean value theorem gives
$$\sqrt{nV(W)}\,\Phi^{-1}(\alpha_n) \geq \sqrt{nV(W)}\,\Phi^{-1}(p)-\sqrt{V(W)}D_\epsilon,$$
and combining this with the coding-to-simulation inequality and Lemma~\ref{lem:new} we obtain that
\begin{align} 
\log M_\epsilon^*(W^{\otimes n}) 
&\geq \log N_{\alpha_n}^*(W^{\otimes n})+\log\delta_n\nonumber\\
&\geq nC(W)+\sqrt{nV(W)}\,\Phi^{-1}(\alpha_n) +\left(b(W)-\frac12\right)\log n-K(E_\epsilon)
    \nonumber\\ 
&\geq G_\epsilon(n) +\left(b(W)-\frac{1}{2}\right)\log n -K(E_\epsilon)-\sqrt {V(W)} D_\epsilon. 
    \label{eq:toreuse}
\end{align}
Taking $b(W)=\frac{1}{2}$, we obtain,
\begin{equation}
\log M_\epsilon^*(W^{\otimes n})\geq G_\epsilon(n)-K_-,
\label{eq:lb_M_nonsingular}
\end{equation}
with $K_-=K(E_\epsilon)+\sqrt{V(W)}D_\epsilon$. 
        
                                                           
                       
                                                                                                          
                     
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
                   
                                                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                          
                 
                                                                                            

    For the upper bound, 
    we apply~\cite[Theorem~2]{Cao_channel_simulation},
    \begin{equation*}
        \log M_\epsilon^*(W^{\otimes n}) \leq I_{\max}^{\epsilon-\delta}(W^{\otimes n}) + \log\log \frac{1}{\delta},
    \end{equation*}
    which holds for any $\delta \in (0, \epsilon)$. Set again $\delta = \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}$ for sufficiently large $n$, and define
$$
\eta_n=\epsilon-\frac1{\sqrt n},\qquad
q_n=1-\epsilon+\frac{B(W)+1}{\sqrt n},
\qquad
\gamma_n^*=nC(W)+\sqrt{nV(W)}\Phi^{-1}(q_n).
$$
Then we have that, eventually, $\eta_n\in(0,1)$, $q_n\in(0,1)$, and
$\frac{\gamma_n^*}{n}\to C(W)>-\log r,$ where the last inequality follows from the results of Lemmas \ref{lemma:capacity_dispersion} and \ref{lemma:capacity_ineq_for_general}.
Hence $\gamma_n^*$ is admissible for Lemma~\ref{lemma:one_shot_ub_general}
 applied to $W^{\otimes n}$. The Berry–Esseen calculation at the end of the proof
 of Theorem~\ref{thm:ub_general}, with error tolerance $\eta_n$, gives
$$
\mathbb P_{W_{x^n}}(i(x^n,Y^n)\geq\gamma_n^*)\leq\eta_n.
$$
Consequently,
$$
I_{\max}^{\eta_n}(W^{\otimes n})\le\gamma_n^*
$$
from which we obtain
    \begin{align}
        \log M_\epsilon^*(W^{\otimes n}) &\leq n C(W) + \sqrt{n V(W)}\Phi^{-1}\left(1-\epsilon+\frac{B(W)+1}{\sqrt{n}} \right) + \log\log \sqrt{n} \nonumber\\
        &\leq n C(W) + \sqrt{n V(W)}\Phi^{-1}\left(1-\epsilon \right) + \log\log n, \label{eq:ub_M_nonsingular}
    \end{align}
    where the last inequality follows from a first-order Taylor expansion of $\Phi^{-1}$, and the fact that $\log\log \sqrt{n} = \log(\frac{1}{2}\log n) = \log\log n - \log 2$, with the constant absorbed into the $O(1)$ term. Combining~\eqref{eq:lb_M_nonsingular} and~\eqref{eq:ub_M_nonsingular} yields the desired result.

label: lemma:capacity_dispersion
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since the capacity-achieving output distribution is unique and the channel is symmetric, the distribution of $i(x, Y)$ under $W_x$ is independent of $x$. Consequently, 
     for every capacity-achieving input distribution $p\in\Pi$, the induced output distribution is $Q$. Moreover, symmetry implies that the conditional information-density distribution under $W_x$ is independent of $x$, with mean $C(W)$. Hence,
$$
U(p,W)
=\sum_xp(x)
  \mathbb E_{W_x}\!\left[(i(x,Y)-C(W))^2\right]
=\operatorname{Var}_{W_{x_0}}(i(x_0,Y)).
$$
Thus both the minimum and maximum of $U(p,W)$ over $p\in\Pi$ are equal. In particular, $V_\epsilon(W)$ is independent of $\epsilon\in(0,1)$.

label: lemma:capacity_ineq_for_general
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma:capacity_ineq_for_general}
    Let $W \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{Y}\mid \mathcal{X})$ be a symmetric channel and $Q(y) = \frac{1}{|\mathcal{X}|}\sum_{x \in \mathcal{X}}W(y\mid x)$ is the capacity-achieving output distribution. Then, 

    $$D(W_{x}\|Q) \geq - \log Q(\mathcal{Y}(x)),$$
    for any arbitrary input symbol $x\in \mathcal{X}$.

label: lem:new
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:new}
Let \(W\) be a symmetric channel with dispersion $V(W)>0$, and write
$$ b(W)= \begin{cases} \frac{1}{2},    &W\;\mbox{is nonsingular},\\ 
                                          0,    &W\;\mbox{is singular}. \end{cases}
$$
For every closed interval $E\subset(0,1)$, there are finite constants $K(E)$ and $n(E)$, depending only on $W$ and $E$, such that
$$
\log N_\alpha^*(W^{\otimes n}) \geq nC(W)+\sqrt{nV(W)}\Phi^{-1}(\alpha) +b(W)\log n-K(E),
$$
for every $\alpha\in E$ and all $n\geq n(E)$.

label: eq:oldbounds
title: Proof
body_md:
As we established in Lemma \ref{lemma:capacity_dispersion}, when the input distribution is uniform the information density has mean 
$C(W)$ and variance $V(W)$. Then the finite-blocklength coding-achievability proofs give bounds of the form
\begin{equation}
\log N_\alpha^*(W^{\otimes n}) \geq nC(W)+\sqrt{nV(W)}\,\Phi^{-1}(\alpha-\rho_n) +b(W)\log n-C,
\label{eq:oldbounds}
\end{equation}
where $C$ depends on $W$ but not on $\alpha$ and $n$, and where
$$0\leq \rho_n\leq \frac{D_W}{\sqrt n} ,$$
for all sufficiently large $n$, with the constant $D_W$ depending only on $W$.
Specifically, in the nonsingular case the lower bound on $N_\alpha^*$ follows from the proof of~\cite[Theorem~53]{polyanskiy:thesis}, 
which gives 
$$\rho_n=\frac{k_3+k_4}{\sqrt n}+e^{-k_1n},$$
and $C=\log k_2$, where the constants only depend on the input distribution and the channel. 
Under the uniform input distribution, nonsingularity implies that
$${\mathbb E}[\operatorname{Var}(i(X,Y)\mid Y)]>0,$$
so some output column contains two unequal positive transition probabilities, and both corresponding inputs have positive posterior probability.
In the singular case, the dependence-testing achievability proof in~\cite[Theorem 245 (248)]{PPV:10}
gives  the above the lower bound on $N_\alpha^*$ with 
$\rho_n=D_W/\sqrt n$, where $D_W$ only depends on $W$.

Now write $E=[\ell,u]$, for some $0<\ell\leq u<1$, and define
$$E'=\left[\frac{\ell}{2},\frac{1+u}{2}\right], \qquad D_E=\sup_{v\in E'}(\Phi^{-1})'(v) =\sup_{v\in E'}\frac{1}{\phi(\Phi^{-1}(v))}<\infty.$$
For large enough $n$, we have $\rho_n\leq\ell/2$, thus both $\alpha-\rho_n$ and $\alpha$ belong to $E'$, simultaneously for every $\alpha\in E$. 
Finally, the mean value theorem gives
\begin{align*} 
\sqrt{nV(W)} \bigl[\Phi^{-1}(\alpha)-\Phi^{-1}(\alpha-\rho_n)\bigr] 
&\leq \sqrt{nV(W)}D_E\rho_n\\ &\le \sqrt {V(W)}D_ED_W. \end{align*}
Substituting this into~\eqref{eq:oldbounds} completes the proof.
